instruction.text: Drag and match the quantifiers to the images.

feedback.correct: The quantifier 'both' is used to refer to two things or people together.
The quantifier 'no' is used to indicate a lack of something.
The quantifier 'many' is used to refer to big quantities.

instruction.text: Match the definitions to the correct quantifiers.

atoms.sound: some, refers to an unknown quantity, typically positively

atoms.b: refers to an unknown quantity, typically negatively, and is also used in questions
atoms.sound: any, refers to an unknown quantity, typically negatively, and is also used in questions

instruction.text: Fill in the gap with the correct quantifier.

atoms.a: ssml: There isn’t. <break time='500ms'/> butter in the fridge.
ssml: There are. <break time='500ms'/> sheep in the field.
atoms.b: There are ((++some any)) sheep in the field.
((Both)) of Remi’s math teachers went to the maths competition over the weekend with the team. The team won ((some)) prizes.
How ((many)) grams of flour is needed to make the cake? There should be ((some)) flour in the cupboard.

instruction.text: Fill in the gap with the correct quantifier.

atoms.a: ssml: Were there. <break time='500ms'/> children in school today?
atoms.b: Were there ((++many both)) children in school today?

atoms.a: ssml: Penelope put on. <break time='500ms'/> of her shoes
atoms.b: Penelope, put on ((++both no)) of her shoes.

atoms.a: ssml: <break time='500ms'/>body wanted to wash the dishes.
atoms.b: ((++No Many))body wanted to wash the dishes.
